drivingQuestion: How can the seller redeem his house when the buyer conceals himself so that the twelve months lapse?
outcomeNote: the mishna records an abuse and Hillel's ordinance answering it, with no argument

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה נִטְמָן יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא חָלוּט לוֹ. הִתְקִין הִלֵּל שֶׁיְּהֵא חוֹלֵשׁ מְעוֹתָיו לַלִּשְׁכָּה, וִיהֵא שׁוֹבֵר אֶת הַדֶּלֶת וְנִכְנָס, אֵימָתַי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה הַלָּז יָבֹא וְיִטּוֹל אֶת מְעוֹתָיו.
segments.en: «MISHNA» «At first,» the buyer «would conceal himself» on the final «day of the twelve-month» period, «in order to» ensure «that it would become his in perpetuity. Hillel instituted that» the seller «would place [ḥolesh] his money in the chamber» of the court «and» that «he will break the door and enter» the house, and «when the other» individual, i.e., the buyer, «will wish» to do so, «he may come» to the chamber «and take his money.»

moves.cueHe: בראשונה היה נטמן יום שנים עשר חודש
moves.summary: buyers used to hide on the last day so that the house would become theirs in perpetuity
moves.about: buyers used to conceal themselves on the last day of the twelve months so that the house would become theirs in perpetuity

moves.cueHe: התקין הלל שיהא חולש מעותיו ללשכה
moves.summary: Hillel enacts that the seller deposits the money in the chamber and takes possession
moves.about: Hillel's ordinance letting the seller deposit the redemption money in the Temple chamber, break the door and enter, the buyer collecting his money when he wishes
